verdict.rationale: MoQ Relay connects arbitrary publishers to subscribers and ships native libraries (Rust, Python and others), so a server-side process can subscribe to live audio and publish its own track. SageOx shows server-side subscribers (live transcription, voice ID) consuming live Opus audio in production. However, no evidence shows an agent publishing synthesized speech back into the session, and there is no session or participant model or agent-specific tooling. Missing for 10: documented agent-participant pattern, evidence of server-side speech publishing back to participants, round-trip realtime latency evidence for conversational use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, a server-side agent joins a session as a participant that receives live audio and publishes speech back in realtime

citations.quote: Browser, desktop, mobile and device clients publish Opus to one relay, which fans out to independent subscribers: an S3 archiver, Zoom Scribe Live transcription, and voice ID.
Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
Dynamic announcements, connecting arbitrary publishers to subscribers.
MoQ delivers WebRTC-like latency without the constraints of WebRTC.
